title: Relaywell: Standby Engine Live, "Tell Me Which Class Goes First"

fields.systemName: EXERCISE — Recorded Line, Boardroom Command Center, ext. 5520

callee.name: Marcus Ellery
callee.label: Clinical Systems Lead, Boardroom command center (speaker)

transcript.speaker: Marcus Thale (Relaywell)
transcript.text: Lakemont, it's Marcus Thale with Relaywell, ticket RW-88213. Am I on speaker? Good. The standby engine is promoted. It went live at 06:00, and every channel shows amber, PULLING. Nothing has gone outbound yet. I want to be clear about that.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Ellery (CSL)
transcript.text: Understood. The Laboratory Manager and the pharmacy manager are both here. What are you pulling, and how fast?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Thale (Relaywell)
transcript.text: I'm draining your source queues into the engine store at about 20,000 an hour. Your systems are still adding roughly 6,000 an hour on top of that, so the sources should be empty around 07:50. That's well before your 10:10 drop. By 07:00 you'll have about 31,000 messages held between my store and what's left at source. I'm not releasing a single channel until you tell me replay, hold or discard for each class.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Thale (Relaywell)
transcript.text: Here are the 06:00 numbers by class. ADT, 319. ORM Orders, 4,140. ORU results, 9,660. Medication administration, 5,980. Charges, 4,030. ELR, immunizations and HIE outbound, 230.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Ellery (CSL)
transcript.text: Anything in there that worries you?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Thale (Relaywell)
transcript.text: Yes. Of the 4,140 Orders, 1,960 are more than four hours old. 138 belong to six patients who were discharged or transferred out since 23:20. And about 700 match Orders your units have already carried out on paper. That's going by the paper order list your HIM team sent me. On the results side, there are 112 results for those same six patients.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Thale (Relaywell)
transcript.text: I can't tell which of those patients you've re-registered on downtime numbers, so that's on your identity check, not my engine. If you replay everything in one go, it all lands in Lakechart at once, stale and out of order.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Ellery (CSL)
transcript.text: Hold everything where it is. Nothing releases until we call it.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Thale (Relaywell)
transcript.text: Holding. I need it class by class, and I need a name next to every discard so I can log it on my end. Your store keeps filling while we talk. So tell me which class goes first, and what happens to the other five.

voiceStyles.Marcus Thale (Relaywell): Man in his 40s, remote engineer who has been up all night. Calm and precise, a little hoarse, typing between sentences.
voiceStyles.Marcus Ellery (CSL): Clinical informatics director, tired but steady, speaking from a speakerphone in a busy conference room.

instructorNote: This is the core replay decision. The CSL should propose a class-by-class plan under IS-14-C section 2, and the IC, CMIO and department heads should approve it. The expected plan: ADT replays first through the identity check. Orders more than 4 hours old, medication Orders and results for discharged patients are held for review. Orders already done on paper are discarded only if the class, count and decision-maker are logged. The LPM validates results before release, charges are held, and HIE outbound replays after ADT. Watch for the LPM confirming that reportable results already went to MDH by phone or fax so they are not sent twice, and for any push to replay everything at once.
